papers.title: Meta-CD: a metagenomic sequencing coverage and depth calculator for target species.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic Coverage and Depth Calculator (Meta-CD) is a convenient, biologist-friendly tool for determining coverage and depth to enhance taxonomic detection, functional profiling, and metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) recovery in metagenomics. It supports experimental design and post-sequencing analysis, modeling how genome size, relative abundance, sequencing depth, and DNA quantity influence detection of target species.
papers.summary: Meta-CD is a new, biologist-friendly tool that calculates sequencing coverage and depth for target species in metagenomic experiments. It helps researchers design experiments and analyze post-sequencing data by modeling how genome size, relative abundance, sequencing depth, and DNA quantity affect detection of target species, thereby improving taxonomic detection, functional profiling, and MAG recovery.

papers.title: Proteo-metabolomic integration identifies stage-specific candidate biomarkers for Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with a prolonged prodromal phase and complex motor symptoms. Despite improved clinical criteria, early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring remain challenging. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma metabolites and proteins show biomarker potential, their utility in predictive models is insufficiently characterized. We employed a secondary computational approach to integrate proteometabolomic profiles from CSF and plasma samples of >1100 Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) participants. Using multi-omics ma
papers.summary: This study integrates proteomic and metabolomic data from over 1,100 Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative participants to identify stage-specific candidate biomarkers for Parkinson's disease. The multi-omics approach reveals distinct molecular signatures associated with different disease stages, potentially improving early diagnosis and disease monitoring.

papers.title: Optimizing a culture-enriched hybrid metagenomics pipeline to assess the AMR footprint of livestock manure in anaerobic digestate.
papers.abstract: The role of environmental samples from livestock production systems, including manure and anaerobic digestate, as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) is likely underestimated because conventional metagenomic approaches can overlook low-abundance ARGs and often lack the resolution to associate these genes with their microbial hosts and co-localized mobile genetic elements (MGEs). We evaluated whether culture-enriched metagenomics (CEMG), with and without antibiotic selection, enhances ARG detection in anaerobic digestate and improves the resolution of ARG-MGE-host associations u
papers.summary: This study evaluates a culture-enriched metagenomics (CEMG) pipeline for detecting antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in livestock manure and anaerobic digestate, showing that it enhances detection of low-abundance ARGs and improves resolution of ARG-host and ARG-mobile genetic element associations compared to conventional metagenomics. The approach provides a more comprehensive view of ARG reservoirs in agricultural environments, which is important for understanding and mitigating antimicrobial resistance spread.

papers.title: Unveiling the mechanism of metabolites derived from gut microbiota in the treatment of acute kidney injury via network pharmacology and bioinformatics.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects a considerable proportion of patients that represents a major challenge for clinical treatment. Gut microbiota metabolites have been reported to attenuate acute kidney injury (AKI), yet their underlying mechanisms remain largely elusive. The present study aimed to explore the protective mechanisms of these metabolites against AKI using.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and bioinformatics to investigate how gut microbiota-derived metabolites protect against acute kidney injury (AKI), identifying key targets and pathways. The findings provide a mechanistic framework for the renoprotective effects of these metabolites, potentially informing future therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: A Critical Synthesis of Machine Learning in Autism Spectrum Disorder Genomic Research: From Transcriptomics to Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent impairments in social communication, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors. This narrative review synthesizes advances in machine learning applications to ASD genomic research through May 2026, spanning gene expression analysis, whole-exome sequencing (WES), non-coding variant interpretation, multi-omics integration, single-cell transcriptomics, epigenetic profiling, and gut microbiome analysis. A purposive, thematic literature synthesis approach was employed, allowing broad coverage o
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes recent advances in applying machine learning to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) genomic research, covering transcriptomics, whole-exome sequencing, non-coding variants, multi-omics, single-cell, epigenetics, and microbiome studies. It highlights how ML approaches are being used to identify patterns and biomarkers across diverse data types, potentially improving ASD diagnosis and understanding of its biological underpinnings.

papers.title: Convergent methodologies in prosthetic joint infection research: integrating transdisciplinary approaches to understand and prevent biofilm-driven failure of orthopaedic prostheses.
papers.abstract: Prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) remain among the most devastating complications of arthroplasty, imposing substantial clinical, economic and patient burdens. Although culture-based diagnostics underpin current clinical practice, PJIs are biofilm-driven infections shaped by taxonomic diversity, spatial organization, host responses and surface interactions, meaning conventional approaches provide only a partial and often decontextualized view of the infection process. We examine how convergent methodologies can transform PJI research by integrating approaches that have traditionally been stud
papers.summary: This review discusses how prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) are biofilm-driven and poorly understood by conventional culture-based diagnostics, and proposes that integrating transdisciplinary approaches—such as genomics, spatial biology, and host-response analysis—can provide a more complete picture of infection processes. It highlights the potential of convergent methodologies to improve understanding and prevention of biofilm-driven implant failure.

papers.title: Benchmarking methods for extracting microbial signal from host-dominated metatranscriptomes.
papers.abstract: Human RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data originally generated for human transcriptome profiling are overwhelmingly dominated by host sequences, yet they often contain a small fraction of non-human reads that can be exploited for microbial detection. When such datasets are repurposed for secondary microbiome-oriented analyses, extracting and accurately classifying this weak microbial signal becomes technically challenging, and no ready-to-use pipeline currently exists. In this study, we evaluate computational strategies for filtering host reads and classifying microbial transcripts in host-dominated
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational methods for extracting and classifying weak microbial signals from host-dominated human RNA-seq data, addressing the lack of a ready-to-use pipeline for repurposing such datasets for microbiome analysis. It evaluates strategies for host read filtering and microbial transcript classification, providing guidance on optimal approaches.

papers.title: Maternal secretor status and human milk oligosaccharides influence the infant gut resistome.
papers.abstract: The infant gut resistome is established early in life and is shaped by perinatal exposures, yet the mechanisms underlying its modulation remain unclear. We combined shotgun metagenomics of fecal samples from 57 one-month-old infants and paired milk samples from 50 mothers in the MAMI cohort to investigate the influence of maternal secretor status on early-life resistome development. Longitudinal follow-up at 6 and 12 months, and also further validation in the independent Lifelines NEXT (LLNEXT) cohort, support our findings. Cesarean section (C-section) was associated with increased antibiotic
papers.summary: This study investigates how maternal secretor status and human milk oligosaccharides shape the infant gut resistome (collection of antibiotic resistance genes). Using metagenomic data from the MAMI cohort and validation in an independent cohort, the authors find that C-section delivery is associated with increased antibiotic resistance genes, while maternal secretor status and milk oligosaccharides influence the resistome composition. The findings highlight early-life factors that could be targeted to modulate antibiotic resistance in infants.

papers.title: Syndromic cholera diagnosis masks diverse causes of diarrhoeal disease in Burundi revealed by portable metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Cholera outbreaks remain a major public-health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, where diagnostic capacity is limited and clinical case definitions are non-specific and re ly heavily on syndromic diagnosis. Rapid identification of Vibrio cholerae is critical, yet cholera-suspected diarrhoea can have multiple infectious causes not captured by targeted diagnostics.
papers.summary: This study used portable metagenomics to analyze diarrheal samples from cholera-suspected patients in Burundi, revealing that many cases were caused by other pathogens rather than Vibrio cholerae. The findings highlight the limitations of syndromic diagnosis and the value of metagenomic sequencing for accurate pathogen identification in outbreak settings.

papers.title: xoxF-linked methanol oxidation signals recur across wetland metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Wetlands are globally important methane-cycling ecosystems, but methanol oxidation remains less frequently emphasized than methane oxidation in community-level metagenomic analyses. Recent studies have highlighted the ecological importance of the lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase XoxF, yet wetland-focused xoxF literature remains comparatively limited relative to marine, freshwater, and other environmental systems. Here, we screened wetland-associated records in IMG/M using methane-metabolism and enzyme-centered queries focused on EC 1.1.2.10/xoxF and related methanol-oxidation annota
papers.summary: This study screens wetland metagenomes from IMG/M for methanol oxidation genes, particularly the lanthanide-dependent xoxF gene, and finds that xoxF-linked methanol oxidation signals recur across diverse wetland ecosystems. The work highlights the ecological importance of methanol oxidation in wetlands, which has been understudied compared to methane oxidation, and suggests that xoxF is a widespread and integral part of wetland microbial methane cycling.

papers.title: Rumen DNA virome plasticity and viral metabolic potential are associated with seasonal adaptation in grazing yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
papers.abstract: As a diverse and abundant component of the rumen ecosystem, viruses interact with other microorganisms and are thought to influence microbial metabolism and host productivity. However, how the rumen virome responds to seasonal fluctuations in extreme environments remains poorly understood. Here, metagenomic analyses were used to investigate temporal dynamics of viral diversity, functional potential, and virus-host associations in the rumen virome of yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau across warm and cold seasons.
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to characterize how the rumen virome of grazing yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau changes between warm and cold seasons. The authors find that viral diversity, functional potential, and virus-host interactions are seasonally plastic, suggesting that viruses may help the host microbiome adapt to extreme environmental fluctuations.

papers.title: Decadal Resampling Reveals Widespread Increases in Soil Microbial Diversity Associated With Nitrogen Deposition.
papers.abstract: Simulated manipulation experiments, such as nitrogen addition to mimic atmospheric nitrogen deposition, are widely used in global change research. However, experimental manipulations may differ from real-world environmental change in their intensity, duration, and co-occurrence, leaving long-term changes in soil microbial communities and soil health insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we resampled soils from 38 forest and grassland ecosystems across eastern China in 2009 and 2019 and assessed microbial taxonomic and functional diversity using shotgun metagenomics. Microbial diversi
papers.summary: By resampling soils from 38 forest and grassland sites across eastern China a decade apart, this study found that soil microbial diversity increased over time, and this increase was associated with nitrogen deposition. The findings highlight that real-world environmental changes can have different effects on soil microbial communities than short-term experimental manipulations.

papers.title: AResKGLM: a graph-grounded language-model framework for interpretable multi-hop antimicrobial resistance reasoning.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens microbiology and microbiome bioinformatics because resistance phenotypes are shaped by interactions among genes, mobile genetic elements, and functional environments across microbial communities. Prioritizing resistance determinants requires models that reason across knowledge graphs (KGs) linking genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes. Existing graph-based methods compress this evidence into scalar scores, whereas large language models can produce explanations not grounded in structured evidence. We developed AResKGLM (Antimicrobial
papers.summary: AResKGLM is a new framework that combines knowledge graphs with large language models to provide interpretable, multi-hop reasoning about antimicrobial resistance, addressing the limitation of existing methods that either compress evidence into scores or generate ungrounded explanations. It links genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes to prioritize resistance determinants with structured, evidence-based reasoning.

papers.title: Comorbidity Mechanism and Management of Chronic Low Back Pain and Major Depressive Disorder: From Neural Circuit Remodeling to Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: This review systematically elaborates multi-system interactive mechanisms underlying comorbid chronic low back pain (CLBP) and major depressive disorder (MDD), synthesizes recent advances in diagnosis, treatment, and management, and proposes precision medicine directions to address clinical challenges, including missed diagnosis, treatment resistance, and poor prognosis.
papers.summary: This review examines the shared biological mechanisms underlying the frequent co-occurrence of chronic low back pain and major depressive disorder, including neural circuit remodeling and multi-system interactions. It synthesizes recent diagnostic and therapeutic advances and advocates for precision medicine approaches to improve management of this challenging comorbidity.

papers.title: The Calcidiscus leptoporus genome reveals vitamin-mediated holobiont interactions.
papers.abstract: Coccolithophores are major marine phytoplankton that contribute to ocean carbon cycling through both organic carbon fixation and calcium carbonate biomineralization, yet the functional basis of their interactions with phycosphere bacteria remains poorly resolved. Here, we present the nuclear genome of the haploid phase of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus, a coccolithophore that calcifies in both life-cycle stages. We combined host genome analysis, genome-resolved characterization of associated bacteria, and a four-month vitamin-manipulation experiment to test how B-vitamin biosynthet
papers.summary: This study presents the nuclear genome of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus and combines it with metagenomic and experimental approaches to reveal that interactions with phycosphere bacteria are mediated by B-vitamin exchange. The findings highlight the importance of vitamin-based metabolic dependencies in marine phytoplankton-bacteria holobionts, with implications for understanding ocean carbon cycling.

papers.title: Metagenome-scale modeling to assess microbiome metabolic complementarity for precision microbiota transplantation therapies.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) holds therapeutic promise beyond recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, but clinical outcomes remain unpredictable and donor-selection strategies remain limited, in part because the role of donor‒recipient metabolic interactions in shaping the post-FMT community remains poorly understood. Here, we leverage metagenome-scale metabolic modeling to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient microbiomes and predict post-FMT community composition. Using MICOM-derived metabolic models, we show that donor genomes whose metabolic f
papers.summary: This study uses metagenome-scale metabolic modeling to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient gut microbiomes, aiming to improve donor selection for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). The authors demonstrate that donor genomes with higher metabolic complementarity to the recipient's microbiome better predict post-FMT community composition, offering a potential precision approach to FMT therapies.

papers.title: Longitudinal development of infant oral ecosystem: salivary metabolomic, bacteriome, and virome dynamics in early infancy.
papers.abstract: This prospective cohort study investigated the longitudinal development of the salivary bacteriome, virome, and metabolome during early infancy. We assessed the associations between oral bacteria, viruses, and metabolites from 10 mother-infant dyads, with oral samples collected at 1 and 2 years of age. Forty saliva and plaque samples underwent untargeted metabolomic analysis, and infant saliva samples underwent metagenomic sequencing. Maternal salivary and plaque metabolomic profiles remained largely stable, whereas infant profiles were clearly separated from maternal profiles and changed with
papers.summary: This study tracks how the infant oral ecosystem develops over the first two years, showing that the salivary metabolome, bacteriome, and virome change dynamically and become distinct from the mother's stable profiles. The findings highlight coordinated shifts in bacteria, viruses, and metabolites during early infancy, providing a multi-omics view of oral ecosystem maturation.

papers.title: Endophytic bacteria associated with turmeric, ginger and white radish exhibit dual roles as producers of antibacterial metabolites and carriers of multidrug resistance.
papers.abstract: The increasing global burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) necessitates the exploration of unconventional microbial niches for novel bioactive compounds. Simultaneously, it is also necessary to evaluate their role in the dissemination of resistant bacteria through the food chain. Endophytic bacteria inhabiting edible plant tissues represent a largely underexplored interface between environmental microbiota and human exposure. In this exploratory study, endophytic bacteria were isolated from fresh rhizomes of Zingiber officinale (ginger), Curcuma longa (turmeric), and Raphanus sativus (whit
papers.summary: This study isolated endophytic bacteria from turmeric, ginger, and white radish, revealing that these bacteria can both produce antibacterial metabolites and carry multidrug resistance genes. The findings highlight edible plant tissues as an underexplored niche where beneficial antimicrobial-producing bacteria coexist with potential reservoirs for spreading antibiotic resistance through the food chain.

papers.title: Causal relationships between oral-gut microbiome and bone neoplasm-related phenotypes: Insights from bidirectional Mendelian randomization.
papers.abstract: The human oral and gut microbiota are the 4 largest microbial communities in the body and play crucial roles in maintaining homeostasis and influencing disease. Observational studies have suggested links between these microbiota and bone neoplasm-related phenotypes, but establishing causality has been challenging due to confounding factors and reverse causality. We conducted a bidirectional, 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study to investigate evidence consistent with a potential causal association between the saliva and gut microbiota and various bone neoplasm-related phenotypes. Geneti
papers.summary: This study used bidirectional Mendelian randomization to investigate potential causal links between oral/gut microbiota and bone neoplasm-related phenotypes, finding evidence for specific microbial influences while addressing confounding and reverse causality. The results suggest that certain microbiota may play a role in bone neoplasm risk, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Mock Communities as Quality Control Materials for Clinical Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables comprehensive detection of a broad spectrum of microorganisms. However, its clinical application faces two major challenges: the development of appropriate microbiome-based biomarkers and the need to ensure the reproducibility and quality of the microbiome analytical workflow. Therefore, we developed four types of bead-based mock communities as standard materials for microbiome analysis and evaluated potential experimental biases arising from nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and validation of four bead-based mock communities intended as quality control materials for clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing. The authors evaluated biases introduced by nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis, providing a standardized resource to improve reproducibility and quality assurance in clinical microbiome workflows.

papers.title: Association between Oral Manifestations and Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease-related Esophageal Diseases: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: This scoping review was conducted to map evidence on associations between oral manifestations and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and its related esophageal diseases, including non-erosive reflux disease, erosive esophagitis, Barrett's esophagus and esophageal adenocarcinoma.
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the evidence linking oral manifestations (such as dental erosion, xerostomia, and oral mucosal lesions) to gastroesophageal reflux disease and its related esophageal conditions, including Barrett's esophagus and esophageal adenocarcinoma. The findings suggest that certain oral signs may serve as indicators of underlying GERD severity, but the evidence is heterogeneous and warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into mechanisms of coral larval settlement induction and inhibition by marine biofilms.
papers.abstract: Biofilms are essential to larval settlement in many marine invertebrates, yet the mechanisms driving settlement induction or inhibition in corals remain poorly resolved. This challenge lies in the vast taxonomic and functional diversity of marine biofilms, making it difficult to identify cues associated with settlement. To address this, we analysed the metagenomes of biofilms used to induce settlement (attachment and metamorphosis) of four broadcast-spawning non-acroporid coral species: Dipsastrea favus, Platygyra sinensis, Echinophyllia aspera and Porites lobata. Biofilms were developed for o
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to investigate how marine biofilms induce or inhibit coral larval settlement, identifying functional and taxonomic features of biofilms associated with these contrasting outcomes across four coral species. The findings provide new insights into the microbial cues and mechanisms underlying settlement, which could inform coral reef restoration efforts.

papers.title: Natural Infection of Domestic Dogs with Raccoon Dog and Fox Amdoparvovirus During a Severe Disease Outbreak.
papers.abstract: Raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV) has been reported in raccoon dogs and foxes, but natural infection in domestic dogs has not previously been documented. During March-April 2026, samples from four affected Dobermann dogs from a kennel near Novi Sad, Serbia, were submitted for laboratory investigation. After negative testing for canine adenovirus, canine coronavirus, herpesvirus, parvovirus, distemper virus, influenza A virus, and leptospirosis, metagenomic sequencing was performed on selected tissues, followed by bioinformatic analysis and targeted RFAV PCR screening of additional outb
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study documents the first natural infection of domestic dogs with raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV), identified in four Dobermann dogs from a kennel in Serbia during a severe disease outbreak. Using metagenomic sequencing and targeted PCR, the authors confirmed RFAV as the likely cause, expanding the known host range of this virus and highlighting the need for surveillance in domestic dogs.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein embeddings and genomic context to fill functional annotation gaps in silage metagenomes, improving coverage of carbohydrate metabolism genes. Applied to 21 silage metagenomes, CAAC achieved high cross-validation performance and expanded annotation of carbohydrate-active enzymes, enabling better interpretation of microbial metabolic potential.

papers.title: Deciphering microbial community dynamics using cross-sectional data-informed NeuralODE.
papers.abstract: Understanding the ecological mechanisms of host-associated microbial ecosystems typically relies on either cross-sectional or time-series data. Cross-sectional analyses are limited in their ability to assess intervention effects, whereas time-series models require dense and informative sampling that is often impractical.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a NeuralODE-based framework that leverages cross-sectional microbiome data to infer microbial community dynamics, overcoming the limitations of traditional time-series models that require dense sampling. The approach enables the assessment of intervention effects and ecological mechanisms from more readily available cross-sectional datasets.

papers.title: Wastewater Metagenomic Reanalysis of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Public Datasets from Türkiye (Ankara and Hatay).
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antimicrobial resistance in microbial communities is a global health concern that leads to millions of deaths each year. Many bacterial pathogens have resistance to multiple antibiotics. Domestic wastewater treatment facilities are reservoirs for antibiotic-resistant bacteria and resistance genes. Wastewater-based epidemiology surveillance is crucial for monitoring antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Türkiye has one of the highest levels of antibiotic resistance with a lack of research on resistomes. This study is a focused reanalysis of publicly available wastewater met
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed public wastewater metagenomic datasets from Ankara and Hatay in Türkiye to profile antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), addressing a gap in resistome research for a country with high antibiotic resistance. The findings highlight wastewater treatment facilities as reservoirs of ARGs and underscore the utility of reusing public metagenomic data for wastewater-based epidemiology surveillance.

papers.title: Land-Use and Depth-Dependent Assembly of Soil Microbiomes Shapes Ecological Functions, Interaction Networks, and Phytopathogenic Communities Across Crop and Orchard Systems.
papers.abstract: Soil microorganisms are essential for nutrient cycling, plant productivity, and soil health, yet the relative importance of land-use and soil depth in shaping agricultural microbiomes remains poorly understood. This study investigated soil microbial communities across uncultivated land, alfalfa fields, crop systems (feed corn and sweet corn), and orchard systems (walnut and quince) in the Hajdúnánás region of Hungary using shotgun metagenomic sequencing and soil physicochemical analyses. Microbial alpha diversity showed limited variation among land-use systems but declined significantly with s
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to examine how land-use type and soil depth shape soil microbiomes across agricultural systems in Hungary. They found that microbial diversity declined with depth and that land-use and depth influenced ecological functions, interaction networks, and the abundance of phytopathogenic communities, with implications for soil health and crop management.

papers.title: Tumor Location and Preoperative Biliary Stenting Shape Gut Microbiome Diversity in Pancreatic Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Recent evidence suggests that gut microbiome plays a role in the development of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and influences treatment response. However, the association of tumor location and preoperative biliary stenting (PBS) with gut microbial composition and diversity remains poorly understood. Methods: Preoperative stool specimens were prospectively collected from patients with PDAC undergoing surgery between March 2020 and July 2021 at the Department of Surgery, Heidelberg University Hospital, Germany. Whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed. Micro
papers.summary: This study investigates how tumor location and preoperative biliary stenting influence gut microbiome diversity in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients. Using whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing of preoperative stool samples, the authors found that both factors significantly shape gut microbial composition, suggesting they should be considered in microbiome studies of pancreatic cancer.

papers.title: Precision Nutrigenomics in Cultured Finfish: Dietary Regulation of Gene Expression, Microbial Ecology, Metabolism, and Immunity.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrigenomics requires a diet-microbiome-host perspective because microorganisms can transform feed substrates, generate bioactive metabolites, compete with pathogens, and modify intestinal and systemic gene regulation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative controlled feeding trials, transcriptomic and targeted gene-expression studies, microbiome analyses, and complementary multi-omic evidence concerning dietary regulations in cultured finfish. The available evidence is concentrated particularly on soybean-derived proteins, lipid-source replacements, selected am
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on precision nutrigenomics in farmed fish, emphasizing the diet-microbiome-host axis and how feed components like soybean proteins and lipid replacements regulate gene expression, microbial ecology, metabolism, and immunity. It highlights the need for integrated multi-omic approaches to optimize aquaculture diets for health and sustainability.

papers.title: Microbial Functional Potentials Differ Among Monospecific and Mixed Moss Biocrusts in an Alpine Sandy Ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Moss-dominated biological soil crusts are associated with carbon and nitrogen cycling in dryland and alpine sandy ecosystems, but functional differentiation among closely related moss species and their mixed assemblages remains unclear. We used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare below-crust soil associated with Didymodon constrictus (Mitt.) K. Saito (D. constrictus) crusts (mossC), ferrugineus (Schimp. ex Besch.) M.O. Hill (D. ferrugineus) crusts (mossF), and visually co-dominated mixed crusts (mossM) in the Gonghe Basin on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Fifteen spatially separ
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare soil microbial functional potential beneath monospecific and mixed moss biocrusts in an alpine sandy ecosystem, revealing distinct functional profiles among crust types. The findings highlight that closely related moss species and their mixtures harbor different microbial functional capacities, which may influence carbon and nitrogen cycling in these environments.

papers.title: Vagococcus changpingensis sp. nov., a Fly-Associated Bacterium with Human Gut Metagenomic Representatives: Genomic and Metagenomic Insights into Its Ecological Distribution.
papers.abstract: The genus Vagococcus comprises Gram-positive bacteria with a broad ecological distribution, yet its diversity and potential links between animal and human habitats remain underexplored. Here, we report two novel fly-associated strains, CY52-2T and CY62-2, isolated from a retail market in Beijing, China. Polyphasic taxonomic analyses demonstrated that they represent a novel species, for which we propose the name Vagococcus changpingensis sp. nov. Large-scale mining of 805 public metagenomes identified two human gut-derived genomes that share > 99.3% ANI with V. changpingensis, extending the kno
papers.summary: This study describes a novel bacterial species, Vagococcus changpingensis, isolated from flies in a Beijing market, and uses genomic and metagenomic analyses to show that closely related genomes are also present in human gut metagenomes, suggesting potential links between fly-associated and human habitats. The findings expand knowledge of Vagococcus diversity and its ecological distribution.

papers.title: KEGG-Based Functional Signatures Complement Taxonomic Profiles Associated with Spontaneous Decolonisation of Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales.
papers.abstract: Understanding the functional potential of the gut microbiota for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) decolonisation is essential for developing novel non-antibiotic strategies to promote their clearance. In a previous study, we identified distinct taxonomic signatures associated with spontaneous CRE decolonisation (DeCol). Here, we aimed to determine whether these taxonomic differences were accompanied by differences in the predicted functional potential of the gut microbiota. Patients were identified from a database of individuals colonised with CRE. We performed Illumina shotgun meta
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the gut microbiota's predicted functional potential, based on KEGG pathways, differs between patients who spontaneously clear carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) and those who remain colonized. The findings indicate that functional signatures complement previously identified taxonomic profiles, offering insights into microbial mechanisms that may promote CRE decolonization and informing non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Lesion-specific oral microbiome signatures and predicted carcinogenic pathways in oral squamous cell carcinoma: a paired-site study in Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma accounts for over 90% of oral neoplasms. Despite therapeutic advances, the lack of reliable, non-invasive biomarkers and delayed diagnosis continues to impede effective clinical management. By combining paired lesion and non-lesion sampling with predictive metagenomics analysis, our study addresses this gap and advances the current understanding of microbiome‒tumor interactions.
papers.summary: This study identifies distinct oral microbiome signatures at tumor sites compared to paired non-lesion sites in Pakistani oral squamous cell carcinoma patients, and uses predictive metagenomics to uncover potential carcinogenic pathways. The findings suggest that lesion-specific microbial communities could serve as non-invasive biomarkers and provide insights into microbiome-tumor interactions.

papers.title: Ecological assembly of mucosal and fecal microbiomes in ulcerative colitis across genes, functions, and species.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with gut microbial dysbiosis, yet the ecological processes underlying community assembly remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates the ecological assembly of gut microbiomes in ulcerative colitis patients, comparing mucosal and fecal samples across genes, functions, and species. It reveals that community assembly processes differ between these niches and are disrupted in disease, providing insights into the ecological mechanisms of dysbiosis in IBD.

papers.title: Multi-layer gut microbiome variation in type 2 diabetes despite preserved higher-order community structure.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) has been consistently associated with alterations in the gut microbiome, although disease, treatment, diet, and other host factors may contribute to the observed patterns. How these associations are organized across different biological levels of the microbial ecosystem remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates gut microbiome variation in type 2 diabetes across multiple biological levels, finding that while specific taxa and functional pathways differ, the higher-order community structure remains largely intact. The results suggest that T2D-associated microbiome changes are layered, with preserved overall ecosystem architecture despite compositional and functional shifts.

papers.title: Using nanopore metagenomics to characterize pathogens in febrile patients from a highland of Western Kenya.
papers.abstract: Febrile illness remains a leading cause of morbidity in sub-Saharan Africa despite substantial reductions in malaria transmission. As malaria positive cases decrease, an increasing number of patients with febrile illnesses test negative for Plasmodium infection, leaving their causes unresolved. As a result of the diagnostic gap, patients receive presumptive antimalarial treatment, unnecessary antibiotics and experience delayed therapy.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore metagenomics to identify potential pathogens in febrile patients from a highland region of Western Kenya, aiming to address the diagnostic gap for non-malarial febrile illnesses. The approach demonstrates the utility of metagenomic sequencing for pathogen characterization in clinical samples from resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Agentic AI for trustworthy synthetic microbial genomics: a perspective on generation, validation, and governance.
papers.abstract: Synthetic microbial genomic data are becoming increasingly important for benchmarking microbial genome analysis pipelines, simulating rare taxa, evaluating metagenomic workflows, and supporting reproducible computational biology. Recent genomic foundation models demonstrate that biological sequences can be modelled at unprecedented scale, with emerging capacity for genome-level interpretation, generation, and design. However, the scientific value of synthetic microbial genomic data depends not only on whether sequences can be generated, but whether they are biologically plausible, computationa
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses the use of agentic AI to generate trustworthy synthetic microbial genomic data, emphasizing the need for biological plausibility and computational validation. It proposes a framework integrating generation, validation, and governance to ensure the data's scientific value and reliability.

papers.title: Genome-resolved insights into hydrocarbon-transforming and nitrate-reducing microbial communities from deep petroleum reservoir cores of the Nashpa Oil Field, Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities from deep subsurface petroleum reservoirs are adapted to hydrocarbon-rich, oxygen-limited, and physicochemically extreme environments. However, genome-resolved knowledge of petroleum reservoir microbiomes from Pakistan remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study provides the first genome-resolved analysis of microbial communities in deep petroleum reservoir cores from Pakistan's Nashpa Oil Field, revealing populations capable of hydrocarbon transformation and nitrate reduction. The findings expand our understanding of subsurface microbial diversity and metabolic potential in extreme, hydrocarbon-rich environments.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into microbial communities of terrestrial mud volcanos: functional diversity of subsurface archaea and bacteria.
papers.abstract: Terrestrial mud volcanoes are surface geological features where fluidized sediments and gasses from the subsurface are discharged along a fracture network providing a window into the deep biosphere. Although mud volcanoes constitute an important source of methane emission from natural environments, their microbial communities responsible for methane cycling remain poorly characterized. Using a metagenomics approach, we investigated the taxonomic composition and metabolic potential of microbial communities in three active mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman mud volcanic province. Despite the volca
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to characterize the microbial communities in three terrestrial mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman province, revealing the taxonomic composition and metabolic potential of subsurface archaea and bacteria, particularly those involved in methane cycling. The findings provide new insights into the functional diversity of deep biosphere microorganisms and their role in natural methane emissions.

papers.title: Exposure-aware multi-omics and artificial intelligence for biomarker discovery and precision prevention in diffuse glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse gliomas are now diagnosed and studied through integrated molecular classification, radiomics, single-cell biology, spatial profiling, proteogenomics, metabolomics, and artificial intelligence. Yet many precision-medicine models still begin at diagnosis and emphasize tumor-intrinsic molecular features, leaving environmental, occupational, lifestyle, microbiome, metabolic, immune, and treatment-related exposures at the margins. This review develops an exposome-informed view of diffuse glioma biomarker discovery. Biomarker discovery is separated from clinical prevention: current evidence
papers.summary: This review argues that diffuse glioma biomarker discovery and precision prevention should incorporate the exposome—environmental, occupational, lifestyle, microbiome, and treatment-related exposures—alongside tumor-intrinsic molecular data. It highlights how multi-omics and AI can integrate exposure data to improve biomarker discovery and prevention strategies, rather than focusing only on diagnosis and tumor features.

papers.title: Decoding the functional diversity of plant growth-promoting bacterial communities in the soils of Western Ghats, Tamil Nadu, India.
papers.abstract: Western ghats in India, one of the world's biodiversity hot spots is the reservoirs of microbial resources having agricultural and industrial significance. However, the diversity of plant growth-promoting microbial communities associated with the plants and soil in the Western Ghats is untapped vault. The current emphasis on natural farming is more depending on the indigenous microbial communities and their metabolic functions towards sustainable one -health. With this background, the present study examines the bacterial diversity of soils from the Western Ghats of Nilgiris, Coimbatore and Din
papers.summary: This study explores the bacterial diversity in soils from the Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot in India, focusing on plant growth-promoting bacteria with potential agricultural significance. It highlights the untapped microbial resources in this region and their metabolic functions relevant to sustainable natural farming and one-health approaches.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites target C5AR1/KDM2A/HCAR3 axis in inflammatory bowel disease: a multi-machine learning algorithms and molecular docking study.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic recurrent disorder. Gut microbiota-derived metabolites regulate intestinal homeostasis, but their molecular mechanisms in IBD remain unclear. Current studies lack systematic "microbiota-metabolite-target" network mining with multi-method validation. This study integrates network pharmacology, three machine learning algorithms, and molecular docking to construct this regulatory network in IBD.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, three machine learning algorithms, and molecular docking to construct a 'microbiota-metabolite-target' regulatory network in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), identifying a novel C5AR1/KDM2A/HCAR3 axis potentially mediated by gut microbiota-derived metabolites. The findings provide a systematic, multi-method framework for understanding how microbial metabolites may influence IBD pathogenesis and offer potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Gut microbiota profiles and potential biomarkers in pre-pubertal females with ADHD.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder with significant sex differences in diagnostic rates; males being diagnosed more frequently than females. Gut microbiota alterations may contribute to ADHD via the microbiota-gut-brain axis. However, previous microbiota studies have predominantly used male or mixed-gender samples, neglecting females with distinct clinical and hormonal profiles. The pre-pubertal period is critical for both neurodevelopment and microbiota maturation. This study investigates gut microbiota characteristics in pre-pube
papers.summary: This study investigates gut microbiota differences in pre-pubertal females with ADHD compared to controls, aiming to identify potential biomarkers. It addresses a gap in research that has largely focused on males or mixed-gender samples, highlighting sex-specific microbial alterations that may be relevant to ADHD pathophysiology.

papers.title: Fighting the invader: strategies against intracellular bacteria.
papers.abstract: Intracellular pathogenic bacteria are often-overlooked agent of chronic, recurrent and difficult-to-treat infections in a context of escalating antimicrobial resistance. By hiding within professional and non-professional phagocytes, adopting dormant or slow-replicative states and rewiring host pathways, these pathogens successfully evade both immune clearance and conventional antibiotic therapy, thus contributing to treatment failure and, potentially, carcinogenesis. Here we synthesise how obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade and persist within host cells, and interpret these
papers.summary: This review synthesizes strategies used by intracellular pathogenic bacteria to invade, persist within, and evade host immune and antibiotic defenses, highlighting their role in chronic, recurrent infections and potential carcinogenesis. It discusses mechanisms of host cell exploitation and dormancy, providing a framework for understanding treatment failure and guiding future therapeutic approaches.

papers.title: Hormone priming and metabolic engineering of phytohormone crosstalk in rice under combined biotic and abiotic stresses: a multi-omics perspective for climate-resilient crop development.
papers.abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is the caloric backbone for more than half of humanity, yet it remains one of the most vulnerable crops to the simultaneous biotic and abiotic stresses exacerbated by climate change. Phytohormone priming and the complex crosstalk networks governed by transcription factor hubs like WRKY, MYB, and NAC serve as the central adaptive mechanism for stress resilience. This review synthesizes how multi-omics integration, including spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, is resolving the molecular architecture of hormonal priming and epigenetic stress memory. We critically evalu
papers.summary: This review discusses how phytohormone priming and crosstalk networks involving transcription factors like WRKY, MYB, and NAC help rice cope with combined biotic and abiotic stresses. It highlights the role of multi-omics approaches, including spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, in uncovering the molecular basis of stress memory and epigenetic regulation, offering a path toward climate-resilient crop development.

papers.title: Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 alleviates sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and enhancing S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) impairs cognitive function and induces hippocampal injury, yet the gut-derived mechanisms underlying these deficits remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study shows that the probiotic Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 can alleviate cognitive impairment caused by sleep deprivation in mice. The mechanism involves remodeling the gut microbiota and enhancing S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation, which helps protect hippocampal function.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration identifies a gut-microbiota-associated plasma metabolite signature for alzheimer disease diagnosis and metabolic pathway targeting.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia, with early diagnosis remaining constrained by the invasiveness and limited accessibility of current biomarkers. The gut-brain axis has emerged as a critical communication network linking intestinal homeostasis with central nervous system function, yet the diagnostic utility of gut-microbiota-associated circulating metabolites in AD remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to identify a plasma metabolite signature associated with gut microbiota that can aid in Alzheimer's disease diagnosis and highlight metabolic pathways for potential therapeutic targeting. The findings support the gut-brain axis's role in AD and suggest a non-invasive diagnostic approach.

papers.title: Probiotic mediated modulation of neonatal health: a meta-analysis of prematurity-related morbidity, jaundice, and respiratory distress.
papers.abstract: Prematurity remains a major contributor to neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with neonatal jaundice and respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) representing two of the most common complications associated with immature hepatic and pulmonary development. Increasing evidence suggests that probiotic supplementation may improve neonatal outcomes through modulation of the gut microbiome, gut-liver axis, and gut-lung axis; however, published findings remain inconsistent. The meta-analysis evaluated the effects of probiotic supplementation on prematurity-related morbidity, with particular empha
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This meta-analysis evaluates the effects of probiotic supplementation on neonatal outcomes, specifically focusing on prematurity-related morbidity, jaundice, and respiratory distress syndrome. The findings suggest that probiotics may improve these outcomes through modulation of the gut microbiome and related axes, though the evidence remains inconsistent across studies.

papers.title: Non-nutritive sweeteners, the gut microbiome, and tumor immunity: evidence hierarchy and a sucralose-centered translational model.
papers.abstract: Non-nutritive sweeteners (NNS) are widely used sugar substitutes and constitute heterogeneous dietary and non-dietary exposures. Human gut microbiota findings vary by sweetener identity, purified compound versus commercial formulation, carrier ingredients, dose, duration, host background, and analytical method. Purified compounds and commercial formulations are therefore biologically non-equivalent. A structured narrative search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection was conducted from database inception through 17 July 2026 without language restrictions. Evidence was organi
papers.summary: This review examines how non-nutritive sweeteners (NNS), particularly sucralose, affect the gut microbiome and tumor immunity, highlighting that purified compounds and commercial formulations are biologically non-equivalent due to carrier ingredients and other factors. The authors propose a sucralose-centered translational model and organize evidence hierarchically to guide future research on NNS-microbiome-immune interactions.

papers.title: Time-dependent shifts in microbiota and metabolites of Yuba under ambient storage: implication for quality deterioration and spoilage.
papers.abstract: Yuba (tofu skin), a high-protein and high-lipid plant-based food, is prone to spoilage at ambient temperatures, but the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to elucidate the dynamic changes in the microbial community and metabolites of Yuba during ambient storage to investigate quality deterioration and identify potential biomarkers for quality control.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the microbial community and metabolites of Yuba (tofu skin) change during ambient storage, revealing time-dependent shifts that contribute to quality deterioration and spoilage. The findings identify potential biomarkers for spoilage, which could inform quality control strategies for this high-protein plant-based food.

papers.title: Fermented fruit waste as a microbiome-active soil amendment: a review of field and greenhouse evidence (2009-2025).
papers.abstract: Fruit residues generated across the global food supply chain constitute a rapidly growing, biologically reactive waste stream that, when left unmanaged, degrades environmental and agricultural quality, whereas controlled microbial fermentation offers a practical means of transforming this waste into stabilized, biologically active soil amendments. This review synthesizes evidence from field trials, greenhouse experiments, and microbiome studies published between 2009 and 2025 to evaluate the agronomic and microbiome-level effects of fermented fruit waste (FFW) as a soil amendment within circul
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from 2009-2025 on using fermented fruit waste as a soil amendment, showing it can improve soil microbiome activity and agronomic outcomes while managing a growing waste stream. It highlights the potential of controlled fermentation to convert fruit residues into stable, biologically active products that benefit soil health.

papers.title: Association between gut microbiota characteristics and therapeutic efficacy of multimodal combination therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus: a secondary analysis of a prospective phase II trial.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) carries a poor prognosis. Although SBRT combined with cadonilimab and lenvatinib has shown encouraging antitumor activity in a prior prospective phase II trial, marked interpatient heterogeneity remains. Gut microbiota may influence antitumor immunity and could help identify patients more or less likely to benefit from this regimen.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiota composition is associated with the efficacy of a multimodal combination therapy (SBRT plus cadonilimab and lenvatinib) in hepatocellular carcinoma patients with portal vein tumor thrombus. The findings suggest that specific gut microbiota characteristics may help predict which patients are more likely to benefit from this treatment regimen, potentially enabling better patient selection.

papers.title: Bidirectional Mendelian randomization between oral microbiota and allergic rhinitis in East Asian populations.
papers.abstract: To investigate the bidirectional causal associations between genetically predicted oral microbial taxa and allergic rhinitis (AR) in East Asian populations.
papers.summary: This study used bidirectional Mendelian randomization to investigate causal links between oral microbiota and allergic rhinitis in East Asian populations, finding potential causal effects of certain microbial taxa on AR risk and vice versa. The results suggest that specific oral bacteria may influence allergic rhinitis susceptibility, highlighting a possible role for the oral microbiome in this condition.

papers.title: Correlation between oral microbiome characteristics and clinical phenotypes in patients with GERD and its changes after anti-reflux surgery.
papers.abstract: Gastroesophageal reflux disease is defined by the reflux of gastroduodenal material into the esophagus, leading to troublesome symptoms and complications. Although the gastrointestinal microbiome has been increasingly implicated in gastroesophageal reflux disease pathogenesis, existing research has largely centered on esophageal and intestinal microbiota. The alterations and clinical relevance of the oral microbiome in gastroesophageal reflux disease remain underexplored. Therefore, this study was designed to: (1) systematically compare the oral microbiome structure between gastroesophageal re
papers.summary: This study compares oral microbiome composition between GERD patients and controls, and examines changes after anti-reflux surgery. It finds correlations between specific oral microbial features and clinical phenotypes, suggesting the oral microbiome may play a role in GERD and could be modulated by surgical intervention.

papers.title: rCCLasso: a robust framework for microbial correlation network analysis reveals age-related microbial dynamics.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome continues to evolve beyond early adulthood, yet most microbiome aging studies focus on changes in individual taxa or overall diversity, leaving microbial interaction dynamics largely unexplored. Correlation-based microbial networks offer an interpretable framework for studying such interactions but are challenging to estimate from compositional microbiome data. Although compositionality-aware methods such as CCLasso provide principled multivariate inference, we identify a previously overlooked limitation: sensitivity to random seeds, which leads to unstable correlation
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This paper introduces rCCLasso, a robust framework for microbial correlation network analysis that addresses the issue of random seed sensitivity in the existing CCLasso method. The authors demonstrate its utility by revealing age-related microbial interaction dynamics in the human gut microbiome, moving beyond individual taxa or diversity-focused studies.

papers.title: Gut microbiome and functional adaptations to paleo and rational diets in professional athletes: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Nutrient-rich dietary patterns are recognized as important modulators of gut microbiota diversity, whereas restrictive diets may increase the risk of microbial depletion and functional imbalance. Among alternative nutritional strategies, the Paleo diet has been considered for its potential applicability in sports nutrition, however, evidence regarding its effects on the gut microbiome remains limited. This study aimed to analyze and compare the taxonomic structure and functional potential of the gut microbiome in professional handball players following an 8-week isocaloric Paleo or rational di
papers.summary: This pilot study compared the gut microbiome of professional handball players following an 8-week Paleo diet versus a rational diet, finding that the Paleo diet was associated with distinct taxonomic and functional changes, though the effects on overall diversity were limited. The results suggest that restrictive diets like Paleo may influence microbial functional potential but require further investigation in athletic populations.

papers.title: HPV vaccination associates with Lactobacillus crispatus-dominant vaginal microbiota in women with cervical lesions: a metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination provides high-level protection against cervical cancer through type-specific antibodies, although breakthrough and persistent high-risk HPV (hrHPV) infections may still occur in some vaccinated women. In addition to neutralizing antibodies, vaccination elicits other immune mechanisms that may influence viral persistence and disease progression. Because mucosal immunity is closely linked to the vaginal microbiota, microbial composition may also play an important role in HPV susceptibility, with Lactobacillus crispatus dominance associated with protection,
papers.summary: This metagenomic study found that women with cervical lesions who had received the HPV vaccine were more likely to have a vaginal microbiota dominated by Lactobacillus crispatus, a species associated with protection against HPV. The findings suggest that HPV vaccination may influence the vaginal microbial environment, potentially contributing to its protective effects beyond generating antibodies.

papers.title: A generalized supervised contrastive learning framework for integrative multi-omics prediction models.
papers.abstract: Advancements in multi-omics research have demonstrated the potential of integrating human microbiome and metabolomics data to better understand physiological processes and improve prediction accuracy in studies of human health. While conventional models utilizing single-omics data provide valuable perspectives, they often fail to capture the complexity of biological systems. Recent developments in supervised contrastive learning frameworks have enhanced predictive performance for categorical responses, yet limitations persist in extending these methods to continuous outcomes. A robust model ca
papers.summary: This paper introduces a generalized supervised contrastive learning framework that extends multi-omics integration to continuous outcomes, addressing a key limitation of existing methods that only handle categorical responses. By integrating human microbiome and metabolomics data, the framework improves prediction accuracy for physiological processes, offering a more robust approach for health-related studies.
